subject: Missed cleavage peptides merged by MSStatsPTM

messages.author: ca31c2295ae7ae58
messages.subject: Missed cleavage peptides merged by MSStatsPTM
parts:
Dear developers,

I realized that since PTM-feature features are relabeled to ProteinAccession+modified sites (e.g.: Q34H12_S12 ) by the SpectronauttoMSstatsPTMFormat converter, peptides indicative of the same phosphosites but differing in their PeptideSequence because of a missed cleavage will be merged according to the "summaryforMultipleRows"-argument. 
For example:
GHILS(Phospho)AAR and GHILS(Phospho)AARK will get summarized since they both point exactly to the same phosphopeptide.
I guess this is an intended behavior? 

Best

Robert

messages.author: 13904eb0f06097b0
messages.subject: Re: Missed cleavage peptides merged by MSStatsPTM
parts:
Hi Robert,

Yes this is the intended behavior. We summarize all peptides spanning the same modification site together (not including peptides with multiple modifications, which are summarized separately). This is why the converter adds the site into the "ProteinName" column and not the whole peptide sequence. If you do want to separate out the missed cleavage peptides you can either filter these out after the converter, or add the peptide sequence directly into the "ProteinName" column before summarization. 

E.g.
input$ProteinName = paste(input$ProteinName,  input$PeptideSequence, sep="_")

Best,
Devon
